messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: repeated container restarts in pool us-west-2-gpu-a (service: runtime-mgr). Crashloop count = 120 in last 5m. Severity: high. Please ack and triage.

alice: acked. saw spike in 500s and node evictions. containers restart immediately.

ben: on it — pulling logs now. can someone confirm if this is segfault or OOM?

carla: logs show SIGSEGV from libfastkernels.so inside runtime loop. stacktrace truncated. snippet below:
```
runtime_engine() at engine.cc:3142
libfastkernels.so(+0x4a3b2) [0x7f3b2a4a3b2]
rax=0x0 rbx=0x7f3b2a000000 rcx=0x7f3b2a4a3b2
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

alice: thanks. no OOM lines in dmesg, GPU memory looks okay per telemetry. CUDA driver reports a device reset on some hosts.

dmitri: node list: n-gpu-05, n-gpu-06, n-gpu-07 showing repeated container restarts. n-gpu-06 also flapped kworker around same time. suspect bad kernel module load or driver hiccup.

ryan: adding core-collection hook to the DaemonSet so we capture full coredumps + nvcrash logs. running: `kubectl exec -n infra debug -- gcore -o /tmp/core.$(pid) $(pid)` fallback.

maria: rolling a temporary traffic split: route 70% to runtime-mgr-v2 (no custom kernel) and 30% to legacy. updating LB weights now.

carla: also enabling automatic model fallback for high-latency requests to reduce pressure on failing pool.

ben: attaching a full `kubectl describe pod` for one failing instance:
```
Name: runtime-mgr-7f9c4
Status: CrashLoopBackOff
Last State: Terminated
  Reason: SignalException
  Exit Code: 139
Events:
  Normal  Killing  2s kubelet killed container with signal 11
```

alice: customer-facing impact: spikes in 502/504 for hosted API routes using large-context models pinned to this pool. CS alerted; some paid workloads affected.

dmitri: immediate mitigations I propose:
- cordon n-gpu-06 and drain with `--ignore-daemonsets`
- scale up warm pool in us-west-2-gpu-b and move traffic
- disable custom kernel path via feature-flag `FASTKERNEL_ENABLE=false`

ryan: started drain on n-gpu-06 (evicting pods). ETA ~3m for drain to complete, may trigger brief throttling.

infra-bot: Cordon applied to n-gpu-06 by ryan at 4861240100. Pods scheduled to other nodes.

carla: can we hot-patch runtime to add null-check guard around that symbol? risky in prod. prefer fallback route.

ben: agreed. quick rollback to runtime-mgr:v1.9.2 (known-good) for the pool, then run canary with v2.0 without libfastkernels. kicking rollout now.

alice: notifying oncall for next shift — dmitri, handing off. full context recorded in thread. dmitri, take lead for post-mortem. :thumbsup:

maria: CS update: notified top 10 affected customers, they're seeing 10-30% increased error rates; we offered credits and a status page note.

dmitri: taking over. timeline: collecting cores, draining suspect nodes, and rolling pool to v1.9.2. will keep this channel for final handoff to infra and forensics.

ben: rollout to v1.9.2 completed on pool us-west-2-gpu-a at 4861240450. crashloops stopped on 8/9 nodes. one remaining pod on n-gpu-07 still restarting — collecting core.

ryan: nvcrash + coredump uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-4861239999/coredumps/ — perms set to incident-team.

carla: quick triage note: stack indicates a race leading to null-deref when a kernel library unloads during concurrent inference teardown. likely a timing window introduced in v2.0 with new batching optimizations.

dmitri: actionable next steps:
- block v2.0 deployment to any gpu pool until fix validated in staging
- add additional safety null-checks in the kernel shim and add regression test covering concurrent unload
- run memory + thread sanitizer on v2.0 build with representative workload
- create follow-up PMR for driver/kernel interactions with vendor

alice: handoff: I am now offshift, leaving dmitri as incident lead. oncall rotation notified.

dmitri: thanks. will produce incident report with customer impact metrics and next steps. estimated mitigation complete at 4861240800.

incident-bot: Incident severity lowered to medium at 4861240865. Monitoring will continue for 2 hours.

maria: CS will send customers a summary and expected follow-up. :white_check_mark: 

ben: leaving notes for postmortem: attach cores, list of nodes affected, rollout artifacts, traffic split logs, and exact git diff of v2.0->v1.9.2.

carla: created ticket INF-9876 for the regression fix and test coverage. assigned to eng-ml team.

dmitri: closing live coordination. will reopen if crashloops resurface. thanks team. :heart:
